entities.summary: Greenlandic: Uunartoq Qeqertaq, English: Warming Island, is an island off the east central coast of Greenland, 550 kilometres north of the Arctic Circle. It became recognized as an island only in September 2005, by US explorer Dennis Schmitt. It was attached to the mainland of Liverpool Land by glacial ice even in 2002, when the ice shelves began retreating rapidly in this area, so that by 2005 it was no longer attached to the mainland. Members of the scientific community believe this newly discovered island is a direct result of global warming. Uunartoq Qeqertaq is a island. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The discovery of Uunartoq Qeqertaq in 2005 highlights the impact of global warming on polar regions, with this newly formed island serving as a tangible example of climate change's effects. Its formation is attributed to rapid ice shelf retreat and subsequent glacial detachment.
